children: Braskem and its main shareholders, including Petrobras, have agreed with creditors to restructure more than $10.9 billion in debt.
The Brazilian petrochemical company's steering committee of creditors said in a filing Tuesday that Braskem would restructure through an updated extrajudicial reorganization plan.

The deal includes a $2.25 billion equity rights offering, of which $1.3 billion will be backstopped by the main shareholders or creditor-approved third parties. It also includes up to $3.6 billion of debt-to-equity conversion.
The third part of the deal is a secured takeback debt for certain creditors. The debt has a 10.5% weighted average interest rate and no maturity or amortization before 2031.
The agreement is subject to confirmation by a court and negotiation of further terms. It doesn't yet constitute an approved transaction.
Braskem and certain creditors have requested the court extend the deadline to submit the updated agreement to allow for time to document it.
